sections.h2: Where a Jessamine County deed is recorded
sections.html:
Deeds for Jessamine County land go to the county clerk's recording desk at the Nicholasville courthouse, 101 North Main Street. Staff are there weekdays, 8 to 4, and the phone is (859) 885-4161.

A second counter operates in Wilmore at 210 South Lexington Avenue, weekdays from 9 until 3. Call ahead to ask which services that branch handles before you carry a closing package there. Nicholasville is the seat and the largest city, which is why most sellers simply use the courthouse.

A house sale usually leaves three papers for the clerk: the deed to the buyer, the lender's payoff release, and sometimes an affidavit. The buyer's title agent expects all of them indexed before funds are released.

Bring these to the counter:

  • The signed, notarized deed with the sale price stated, because the deed tax is figured from that number.
  • A check for the recording charge and the tax. KRS 64.012 also lists a $5 charge when the clerk notarizes the deed on the spot.
  • The lender's release, if it has not been filed. The posted minimum for a release is $46.

The county's clerk page also carries an open records request form for anyone who needs copies later.

A deed starts at $50 and a mortgage at $80. Phone ahead for the current total before writing a check.

Documents past five pages add $3 per extra page, and a mortgage adds the same amount after page thirty. The state's base figure in KRS 64.012 is $33 for up to five pages, so the clerk's totals stack other charges on top. Treat any posted number as a starting point.

The seller owes 50 cents on each $500 of the price written in the deed, and a leftover amount counts as a full $500 block. The clerk collects it at the counter, and a deed isn't accepted for recording until it is paid. Only one county collects the tax on a sale, the one holding the land.

KRS 142.050 excuses a long list of transfers. A few matter to ordinary households:

  • Husband and wife swaps, and transfers between ex-spouses as part of a divorce.
  • Parent and child, or grandparent and grandchild, for a token payment.
  • A corrective deed that fixes one already of record.
  • A foreclosure, or a surrender of the home to the lender in lieu of one.
  • A deed that only pledges or frees property as security for a loan.

If a deed is a gift and no exemption fits, the clerk uses the likely open-market price instead.

You can, with a subscription. The clerk runs eCCLIX for viewing and printing indexed documents, and four vendors are listed for electronic recording. Inside the office, the same records can be viewed at no charge.

Deeds, mortgages and wills are indexed from June 30, 1966, and scanned images online cover most filings since January 2004. For an old boundary question or a decades-old lien, start with the in-office index.

  • eCCLIX: login issued by the site administrator, with charges for data and images.
  • Indecomm: (704) 412-3179.
  • CSC: (866) 652-0111.
  • Simplifile: (800) 460-5657.
  • ePN: (888) 325-3365.

Another tool is DOCALERT, a free email notice that fires whenever a deed or mortgage is filed under a name you register. People who own inherited or empty parcels in the county get the most from it, because a bogus filing is simpler to challenge when caught within days.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill after recording
sections.html:
The county Property Valuation Administrator picks up the transfer and changes the owner of record. The sheriff, not the clerk, sends the bill, and the clerk returns to the picture only if a bill stays unpaid.

The age 65 homestead exemption is attached to the owner, not the parcel. If you sell, tell the PVA's office so the credit leaves the old address. The exemption is $49,100 for 2025 to 2026.

After April 15, unpaid bills move to the clerk, whose website has a delinquent tax search. One percent monthly interest and commissions begin at that point. If you have an old unpaid bill, settle it before signing the deed, and the clerk can quote the payoff.

sections.h2: Other clerk services around a move
sections.html:
The same clerk who records the deed also runs several services a seller touches around a move. Deeds and mortgages, delinquent taxes, notary commissions, voter registration and vehicle registration are all clerk services.

  • Voter registration: a change of address after the sale goes through the clerk's election department.
  • Vehicle registration renewals: the clerk's site offers a renewal tool that asks for a title number, a plate number and a card.
  • Delinquent tax lookups: the clerk's site links to a search, and the clerk alone sets the dollar amount owed at the time of payment.
  • Land records: eCCLIX covers last-minute title follow-ups, estate settlements and appraisals.

Wills and affidavits of descent are recorded at the same counter, at the $47 and $50 starting charges. An heir listing an inherited house in Jessamine County should ask the clerk which of those papers the title company will want on record.

The county gained roughly 4,000 residents between the 2020 count of 52,991 and a July 2025 estimate of 57,147, a rise of 7.8 percent. There are 22,061 housing units, and 512 building permits were issued in 2025. Nicholasville and Wilmore are the two cities, and the county belongs to the Lexington-Fayette metro area.

Two thirds of homes, 66.7 percent, are lived in by their owners. The median home value is $268,100, and households earn a median of $74,576. New subdivisions and former farm tracts keep the clerk's counter busy with plats, easements and survey references, each recorded as its own item with its own fee.

Before closing day, confirm the deed shows the real sale price, since the tax is figured from it. Have the notary sign off, and ask the title agent whether the lender's release has been filed. If your mortgage is being paid off, the release is $46 at the posted minimum.

A cash sale follows the same recording steps. The deed still needs the tax paid, and any old tax bill or lien still needs to be cleared. Keep the receipt from the clerk, and sign up for DOCALERT if you want an email whenever something is filed under your name later.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed for a Jessamine County house?
faqs.a: The Jessamine County Clerk. Go to the courthouse at 101 North Main Street in Nicholasville or call (859) 885-4161.

faqs.q: Why is the clerk's recording charge higher than the state fee?
faqs.a: KRS 64.012 sets $33 for a short instrument, while the clerk's page starts a deed at $50. Check the current total with the clerk.

faqs.q: Who pays the Kentucky deed tax on a sale?
faqs.a: The seller. State law puts it on the grantor, 50 cents per $500 of stated value, collected by the clerk at filing.

faqs.q: Is there a way to learn when a deed is filed under my name?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk offers DOCALERT, a free email alert for deeds and mortgages recorded under a registered personal or business name.

faqs.q: How far back do the Jessamine County deed indexes go?
faqs.a: To June 30, 1966, for deeds, mortgages and wills. The indexes are free to view at the clerk's office, or by eCCLIX subscription from home.
